newsitem.title: USA: Intel shares fall on revenue outlook.
newsitem.headline: Intel shares fall on revenue outlook.

text.p: Intel Corp shares fell Tuesday after the world's biggest computer chip maker forecast slowing revenue and falling gross margins in coming quarters.

The company said Monday its first-quarter net income more than doubled, beating most Wall Street forecasts. But Intel said it expects revenue in the second quarter -- when personal computer sales traditionally have picked up from the after-Christmas lull -- to rise only slightly.
Intel shares, the most active in U.S. markets, were down 4-1/2 at 129-1/4 in midafternon trading of 18 million shares.

"With higher interest rates, there's a huge overhang on stocks like Intel," said Jim Poyner, analyst at investment bank Oppenheimer & Co in New York. "The notion that their revenue is going to be flat in the second quarter is all it takes for people to dump it."

Intel also said the number of chips it shipped in the first quarter was relatively flat compared with the 1996 fourth quarter. That means its new line of Pentium microprocessors, with better multimedia capabilities, did little to encourage sales of personal computers, analysts said.
Still, Intel reported first-quarter net income of $1.98 billion, or $2.20 a share, far more than most analysts were expecting.

Intel said demand for its new high-end chips, including the Pentium Pro and Pentium with MMX, was strong. Company executives also said they expect strong demand for the Pentium II, scheduled to be introduced in May.

Intel is notorious for giving conservative outlooks, some analysts said. Based on the strong demand for existing and upcoming chips, at least three analysts increased their 1997 earnings forecasts for the company.
"Intel's being conservative because of the transition from Pentium Pro to Pentium II," Poyner said. "I don't view it as any kind of a shock" to demand for its products.
